quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Anfernee Simons' playmaking and passing development
quotes.excerpt: very good passer as we saw, and even with his late passes and his lob stuff
quotes.quote: Defense downhill, very good passer as we saw, and even with his late passes and his lob stuff that he is seeing late to Rob, but I thought the, you know, from a first game again, it's you're only one and zero, but I thought that everybody just contributed, tried to play the right way, and even that that that last group tried to as well and I just appreciate it.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praised Anfernee Simons for his playmaking and passing development in the season opener, noting that he is seeing the floor well and making the right reads.

structured.context: Head coach Micah Nori discusses Anfernee Simons' playmaking and passing development following a win.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Toumani Camara's improved catch-and-shoot three-point shooting
quotes.excerpt: his catch and shoot threes in our practice facility since Labor Day is like 52 percent
quotes.quote: You are talking about guys getting easier looks on their playing off ball. Toumani had a lot of quiet threes tonight. He was knocking down his. Is that something that you hope to unlock more with him this year as opposed to some of the harder shots he had to create for himself last year? Absolutely. I mean, you guys all know this, the game is so analytical now. No putting pressure anything or knock on Toumani, but his catch and shoot threes in our practice facility since Labor Day is like 52 percent. So I don't think it's an aberration, but absolutely.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says Toumani Camara is shooting 52 percent on catch and shoot threes in practice since Labor Day, suggesting his improved perimeter shooting is no aberration.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses Toumani Camara's improved catch-and-shoot three-point shooting performance.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the impact of Damian Lillard's gravity on teammates
quotes.excerpt: the magnitude that which Dame pulls guys when he's off the ball, Toumani and those guys are going to get
quotes.quote: Again, I hate to keep going back to it, but this is what we talked about, what we knew. When you have decision makers and you got guys can can draw a crowd, and obviously the magnitude that which Dame pulls guys when he's off the ball, Toumani and those guys are going to get nice open looks. I thought Scoot, even though he was one for five in the first half, I thought every single one of those were good looks as well. But I think that absolutely, Toumani, even City, and these guys are going to be able to catch and shoot, shoot all of them, quite honestly. I hope they do.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori highlights the gravity Damian Lillard provides, noting that when he draws a crowd, teammates like Toumani Camara and Scoot Henderson are going to get open looks.

structured.context: Micah Nori explains how Damian Lillard's gravity on the court creates open opportunities for his teammates.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the emotional significance of his first win as head coach
quotes.excerpt: it exceeded them, never in my wildest dreams did I think that we were going to have the start
quotes.quote: We were waiting 28, 29 years for this moment, Micah. What does it mean to have this game and did it kind of meet your expectations? It exceeded them, never in my wildest dreams did I think that we were going to have the start we did and and and play as well as we did and win by as many as we did. But yeah, it exceeded expectations from a sense that you just appreciate the guys and how much it actually and and you felt it and how much it meant to them for me and and and the staff and all that.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says his first win as head coach exceeded his expectations, adding that he truly appreciates how much the team played for him and the staff.

structured.context: Micah Nori reflects on the emotional significance of winning his first game as a head coach.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on his family's presence at his coaching debut
quotes.excerpt: for them to be here and for me to look up and then just my brothers and sisters
quotes.quote: With your parents being here and such a big night, it's a chance for reflection. What what type of things did you go back and think of or did anything get a pop up? Yeah, a lot, everything. I think when I look up there and you have an 84-year-old dad and an 82-year-old mom and they're able to fly all the way to Portland from Middletown, Ohio and take a connecting flight through Phoenix, which my mom should never be a travel agent, but for them to be here and for me to look up and then just my brothers and sisters and nieces and nephews and everybody, it means a lot. We have a very close family and for them to be here meant the world and obviously my wife Melissa being here meant the world.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori reflected on the emotional significance of his coaching debut, noting that having his parents and family in attendance meant the world to him.

structured.context: Micah Nori talks about the presence of his parents and family at his coaching debut.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on his family's support and his daughter's absence
quotes.excerpt: Dante was playing in an Arizona Fall League game and my daughter, she's a freshman in South Carolina
quotes.quote: You mentioned your nieces and that's why I wondered, I didn't see, yeah, so yeah. Yeah, so they were the only ones that come out here. Dante was playing in an Arizona Fall League game and my daughter, she's a freshman in South Carolina, so she's got classes tomorrow, but it was it was good. I know they all were watching and I just I appreciate it.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori explained that his daughter could not attend his coaching debut because she had classes at school.

structured.context: Micah Nori explains which family members were able to attend his debut and which were watching from afar.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the team's performance and the quick turnaround
quotes.excerpt: to draw it up the way Dame came back and the way he played and the way Ja
quotes.quote: Your clothes look dry, taking you haven't gone in the locker room yet? No, I already did and I changed and it was a it was a cold shower when they in the guys, it was the best cold shower I've gotten. But it was good and like I said, when you look back and I know it's only one game, but to draw it up the way Dame came back and the way he played and the way Ja, his first game and you go down the list the way Drew, I mean, I could name every single one of them and just if you could bottle this and carry this forward for 82, then I think that would be any coach's dream, but we know it, there's a big one in Sac that we got in two days, which is the great thing about the NBA, they just keep coming at you.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praised the team for their collective performance in the opener, saying if they could bottle this effort and carry it forward for 82 games, it would be any coach's dream.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the team's performance and the quick turnaround before their next game against Sacramento.
